# Chapter 14: Enterprise Deployment and Management

Managing Linux across thousands of developer laptops, on-premises virtualization clusters, and multi-region cloud accounts requires enterprise-grade identity federation, automated compliance auditing, zero-downtime kernel patching, and centralized fleet monitoring.

Ubuntu 26.04 LTS integrates modern enterprise toolchains: **`authd`** for cloud identity federation (Google Cloud IAM, Microsoft Entra ID, and OIDC), **`ADSys`** for Active Directory Group Policy management, **Canonical Landscape** for fleet orchestration, and **Ubuntu Pro** for 12-year compliance automation.

This chapter details the deployment, identity integration, fleet operations, and forensic incident response workflows required in enterprise environments.

---

## Ubuntu Pro: The Enterprise Maintenance Engine

Ubuntu Pro transforms the standard operating system into an enterprise-supported platform:

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        UBUNTU PRO COVERAGE MATRIX                      │
│                                                                        │
│   Component               Standard Ubuntu       Ubuntu Pro             │
│   ─────────────────────   ───────────────       ──────────             │
│   'Main' Repository       5 Years Updates       10–12 Years (ESM)      │
│   'Universe' (35k pkgs)   Best-effort / None    10–12 Years (ESM)      │
│   Kernel Patching         Requires Reboot       Livepatch (Zero Reboot)│
│   FIPS 140-3 Cryptography Not certified         FIPS Validated Modules │
│   Compliance Automation   Manual                USG Tooling (CIS/DISA) │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Automate fleet enrollment via configuration management (Ansible / cloud-init):
```bash
sudo pro attach <TOKEN> --no-wait
sudo pro enable livepatch esm-apps esm-infra fips-updates
```

---

## Zero-Downtime Kernel Patching with Canonical Livepatch

Livepatch patches running kernel code in memory without restarting daemons or disconnecting active TCP sessions:

```bash
# Verify Livepatch connectivity and applied fixes
canonical-livepatch status

# Check if immediate reboot is ever required
canonical-livepatch kernel-upgrade-required
```

Under the hood, Livepatch utilizes the kernel's `ftrace` and livepatching infrastructure (`CONFIG_LIVEPATCH`), redirecting function calls dynamically to patched memory blocks without race conditions.

## Centralized Fleet Management with Canonical Landscape

**Landscape** provides a web console and API for orchestrating Ubuntu instances:

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                     CANONICAL LANDSCAPE TOPOLOGY                       │
│                                                                        │
│   ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │               Landscape SaaS / On-Prem Controller              │   │
│   │      (Web UI, REST API, Role-Based Access, Package Mirrors)    │   │
│   └──────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┬──────────────┘   │
│                  │                                  │                  │
│       TLS Port 443 / Message Broker      TLS Port 443 / Message Broker │
│                  │                                  │                  │
│                  ▼                                  ▼                  │
│         [ Workstation Fleet ]               [ Cloud Instance Fleet ]   │
│         landscape-client daemon             landscape-client daemon    │
│         (Desktop GPO / Inventory)           (Auto-Patches / Security)  │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Enroll a client node:
```bash
sudo apt install -y landscape-client
sudo landscape-config --account-name enterprise --registration-key secretkey \
    --computer-title "laptop-alice" --ping-url https://landscape.corp.com/ping
```

## Cloud Authentication with `authd`

Legacy Linux identity required maintaining complex LDAP or Kerberos infrastructure. Ubuntu 26.04 LTS introduces **`authd`**—a cloud-native authentication broker developed by Canonical:

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                      AUTHD CLOUD IDENTITY FLOW                         │
│                                                                        │
│   1. User types corporate email at GDM login: alice@corp.com           │
│   2. authd initiates OIDC device code flow or SAML challenge           │
│   3. User approves on mobile device / MFA with Entra ID or Google IAM  │
│   4. Cloud Identity Provider returns signed JWT / ID Token             │
│   5. authd verifies token signature against IdP public JWKS keys       │
│   6. authd creates local POSIX user & home directory dynamically!     │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Configure `/etc/authd/authd.yaml`:
```yaml
provider: oidc
issuer: "https://login.microsoftonline.com/tenant-id/v2.0"
client_id: "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
domains:
  - "corp.com"
default_groups:
  - "users"
  - "developers"
```
Restart `authd`:
```bash
sudo systemctl restart authd.service
```

## Active Directory Integration with `ADSys`

For environments with existing Microsoft Active Directory domains, **ADSys** extends native Windows Group Policy Objects (GPO) to Ubuntu clients:

```bash
# Join machine to corporate Active Directory domain
sudo realm join -U Administrator corp.local

# Install ADSys client
sudo apt install -y adsys

# Apply Group Policies (dconf settings, proxy rules, privilege boundaries)
sudo adsysctl update -v
```

System administrators can manage desktop wallpaper, password policies, AppArmor restrictions, and network proxies directly from Windows Group Policy Management Console (`gpmc.msc`).

## Patch Management and Compliance Automation

Schedule controlled update rings across staging and production server fleets:

```bash
# Stage 1: Check security vulnerabilities with unattended-upgrades dry-run
sudo unattended-upgrade --dry-run --debug

# Configure automatic application of security updates only in
# /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/50unattended-upgrades:
#   Unattended-Upgrade::Allowed-Origins {
#       "${distro_id}:${distro_codename}-security";
#   };
```

---

## Security Incident Response and Forensics

When a server is suspected of being compromised, execute rapid forensic triage:

```bash
# 1. Capture volatile memory and process state without rebooting
sudo ss -tulpne > /tmp/forensics-sockets.txt
sudo ps auxwwf > /tmp/forensics-procs.txt
sudo lsof -i -P -n > /tmp/forensics-open-files.txt

# 2. Check for modified system binaries against package database
sudo debsums -s 2>&1 | tee /tmp/corrupted-binaries.txt

# 3. Inspect auditd security audit logs for unauthorized privilege escalation
sudo ausearch -m USER_AUTH,USER_CMD -ts today

# 4. Check systemd unit file integrity
sudo systemctl verify /etc/systemd/system/*
```

## Chapter Summary

- Ubuntu Pro provides up to 12 years of security updates and zero-downtime kernel livepatching.
- Canonical Landscape delivers centralized monitoring, package distribution, and script execution across thousands of nodes.
- `authd` enables passwordless, cloud-native OIDC identity federation with Microsoft Entra ID and Google Cloud IAM.
- `ADSys` brings native Active Directory GPO policy enforcement to Linux client workstations.
- Structured patch rings and automated forensic verification maintain enterprise security posture.
